node.label: E. H. Carr
node.description: A historian of Soviet Russia and of international relations whose What Is History? (1961) became the standard British introduction to historical method. Carr argued that historians select and give meaning to facts through their questions, so that research and interpretation proceed together; his position was long read as a challenge to objectivist history. G. R. Elton’s The Practice of History (1967) was written in open opposition, and John Tosh called the Carr–Elton controversy the best starting point for debate about the standing of historical knowledge. Richard Evans wrote In Defence of History (1997) because Carr’s and Elton’s books were still the standard textbooks and, in his view, inadequate for later debates. The Twenty Years’ Crisis (1939) belongs to his work on international relations, and his History of Soviet Russia began with The Bolshevik Revolution (1950).
